items.value: Twelve notes preserve diagonal conventions, singular SNR endpoints, label nonuniqueness, the printed sketch dimension, iteration/degree accounting, algorithm probability and parameter scope, primed-constant text-layer errors, the integer Holder convention, rectangular label typos, Gaussian-noise independence and the distinction between low-degree results and runtime conjectures.

value.note: Graphon and co-membership losses sum only i<j and divide by binomial(n,2); rectangular loss sums every entry and divides by n1*n2. The source defines Mf_ij=f(xi_i,xi_j) while the sampling model sets diagonal zero; the distinction does not affect off-diagonal loss.

T1,T6 take a supremum over fixed parameter matrices; T2,T5 and T7 average over their stated priors and observation noise. T4 additionally supremizes over arbitrary iid latent-position distributions. Do not introduce balanced labels or a uniform latent law into these scopes.

The model permits q=0 and p=1, but the finite SNR ratios use q(1−p) in the denominator. Nontrivial ratio statements require a positive denominator; the source gives no boundary division convention. T5’s target additionally requires p>q.

The source asserts unique zM even though simultaneous label permutations leave M unchanged. The off-diagonal co-membership matrix ZM is uniquely determined when p>q. The displayed relation for Mij is interpreted off diagonal, as required by the model’s zero diagonal.

Algorithm1 prints B∈R^(p×r), where p is a connectivity probability. Matrix multiplication by the n×n transformed adjacency requires B∈R^(n×r). Preserve the printed source and flag this dimensional typo separately.

T3 sets integer iteration counts t1=t2=C-prime log n without a rounding convention. The printed total degree bound2 t1 t2 misses terms from the displayed recurrence: the generic degree upper bound is 2(t1+1)t2+1 in A,Lambda,B and 2t1t2+1 in A alone with the auxiliary randomness fixed. Both remain O(log²n).

T3 denotes probability by the signal-prior symbol PSBM although its event also involves sampled adjacency and independent Lambda,B. Record the natural joint experiment and this notation ambiguity. The surrounding prose says any p,q∈[0,1], while the referenced prior was introduced under q<p; no unproved scope extension is made.

The PDF’s text layer misreads C-prime,C-double-prime and c-prime as C1,C2 and c1. The census follows the visually printed primes in T3 and T6, preserving the different roles of tuning constants and output constants.

The printed Holder norm uses floor(gamma) derivatives and exponent gamma−floor(gamma), including exponent0 when gamma is an integer. It works on the lower triangle; boundary derivative interpretation is implicit. Do not replace it with another standard Holder convention or silently assert additional boundary extensions.

The parameter-space displays use Q_(zi,zj) while defining separate vectors z1,z2. The prior then prints both vectors as length n, but explicitly indexes rows by n1 and columns by n2. Preserve these typographical inconsistencies and resolve the intended row/column indices separately.

Both row and column labels in PBC are uniform over min(k1,k2), not separately over k1 and k2. The additive observation model states iid standard Gaussian noise; independence from the random signal is the usual intended model but is not separately explicit in that sentence.

The theorems prove lower bounds for degree-constrained polynomial estimators. Equivalence to all algorithms of a given runtime is a conjectural interpretation; the source itself discusses failures of low-degree predictions for certain other problems. No universal runtime lower bound is recorded as proved.

value.note: The source defines elliptical laws via a Lebesgue density and assumes finite mean/covariance. Population whitening requires nonsingular covariance; sample whitening requires invertible sample covariance, which in the absolutely continuous case needs n>d. No pseudoinverse or ridge correction is in the original theorem definitions.

Arctan(0,0) is undefined and direction is undefined at radius zero. The claimed global chart bijection fails at poles, where multiple angle vectors describe the same direction, and at excluded latitude endpoints. Use the printed formulas and record the need for regular-coordinate or almost-everywhere conventions; do not invent a global inverse.

The finite tensor inner-product display uses tilde-alpha-r with tilde-f-s in its last second-sum term. Preserve this printed mismatch. Star denotes an influence derivative, asterisk an adjoint; Gamma’s outer tensor acts on the tensor RKHS rather than directly between the two base RKHSs.

Theorem1 quantifies over all probability measures without separately stating kernel measurability or embedding integrability. Theorem2 assumes Frechet differentiability and (5.11), but does not explicitly list the influence element’s square integrability, covariance trace or Hilbert-space empirical-process conditions needed for a CLT. Record the printed result; do not certify that the hypotheses suffice.

The source calls A:F→H linear even though F is a class of probability distributions and uses A(F−F0). The signed-measure tangent domain and exact multivariate uniform metric are implicit. The influence formula uses contamination directions; it is not an adjoint operation.

Theorem3 refers to Gamma and gives two spectral/local-shift conditions without explicitly restating Theorem2’s assumptions or specifying a triangular-array CLT under local alternatives. Its shifted-normal mean sigma_j/sqrt(lambda_j) is undefined at zero eigenvalues unless a separate convention is provided; none is printed. Do not silently require all eigenvalues positive or drop null-space shifts.

Equation(7.1) prints E[kappa_Theta] while (3.1) and (3.3) use E0 under the fixed spherical angular law. Off the null these differ, so the printed known-parameter statistic may have a different population target from Sigma_UTheta in Theorem4. Preserve the discrepancy; do not silently replace E by E0 or impose the null on the theorem.

The trace-of-AA* definition gives the Hilbert-Schmidt norm. The claimed equivalent supremum on page8 is restricted to simple unit tensors and generally gives the operator norm instead. Retain the original norm used in the theorem statements and flag this explanatory mismatch.

Assumption2 prints v∈S without a dimension and leaves the quantifier on lambda unstated. Its intended meaning is every unit direction and all real lambda; preserve the printed inequality and record the missing explicit conventions. Assumption3 is c^d, not c*d.

Assumption4 is a bound on RKHS feature differences, with the angular feature composed with g and scaled by d^−1. It is distinct from C² bounded-Hessian condition(5.11), and can be affected by chart discontinuities. Do not infer it merely from scalar-kernel smoothness or from choosing a Gaussian kernel.

Theorem4 does not explicitly quantify t; its tail-bound interpretation uses t≥0 and positive kernel bound product. Theorem5 explicitly quantifies epsilon>0 but leaves the nonnegative tail parameter u implicit. Absolute constants are independent of n,d. Reused c1,c2 in Assumption1 and (7.6) should not be assumed numerically identical without further source information.

Theorem6 uses log n≺d≺n^(1/4) without a separate definition of ≺ in the inspected main text; interpret as vanishing ratios for the stated asymptotic regime and retain the original notation. The convergence compares a sequence of norms with a possibly dimension-dependent target, not necessarily a fixed limiting real number. It inherits Theorem5’s assumptions, not its rate functions as premises.

The source refers to g as (2.6) on page7 although g is the inverse (2.7). Coordinate sections assume nonsingular Gram matrices; the displayed final m-hat formula uses e_j in an unsummed first term. Equation(4.5) ends its product at d−2 although (4.3) has d−1 factors. These implementation issues do not authorize changing the population/statistic definitions, and simulation ridge adjustments are not theorem assumptions.

Theorem1 takes open bounded convex U but writes closed endpoint intervals for fibers. The essential-variation supremum uses strict interior points, so no endpoint value is selected by it. For d=1 the projected space is R^0 with its usual singleton measure convention, implicit in the source; no special case is printed.

The fixed-length Delta operator sets the final entry to zero and is then iterated literally. For order2 its penultimate entry is minus the last first difference, whereas the shrinking-row matrix D^(2) omits that boundary term. The source calls(6) and(7) equivalent; retain the discrepancy and pin theorem definitions to the explicitly referenced matrix formulation(7).

N=n^(1/d) must be integral and sufficiently large relative to k+1 for the displayed difference matrices. KTV and discrete Sobolev balls constrain seminorms, leaving the max-degree polynomial null space unbounded. The 1/n risk terms represent finite-dimensional components and must be retained.

Theorem2 bounds left singular vectors in R^r by mu/sqrt(n), exactly as printed, with an arbitrary exceptional set I. Its rate constants hide fixed noise scale. Theorem3 uses Theorem2 in its proof; this is not a new explicit incoherence premise on the KTF signal or an import of generic D into its statement.

Theorems2–3 state OP bounds on squared estimation error, whereas Theorems4–6 concern expected minimax risk. A pointwise in-probability bound alone does not certify a uniform expectation-risk upper bound. Preserve the paper’s stated attainment conclusions without claiming an independent proof of those transitions.

The classes are defined for positive radii. Theorem5’s expression C_n^2*log(1+n/C_n^2)/n needs a limiting convention at zero, and its tau scaling can fall below1 for sufficiently small radii. Q must be an integer-index subset of [N]^d, retain the polynomial null space, and have feasible truncation; rounding/clipping conventions are implicit rather than printed.

Theorem6 first includes 1/n, then reports the canonical rate L_n^(2/(2s+1))*n^(−2s/(2s+1)) without that term or an explicit lower restriction on L_n. This simplification requires the displayed nonparametric term to dominate 1/n; for very small L_n, retain the earlier full rate. Do not repair its final original sentence.

The alternative observation law averages a uniform latent permutation. Aligned edge pairs are iid only conditional on that permutation; the two observed graphs are not independent under the alternative. Negative correlation is allowed only within the Bernoulli feasibility interval, despite the squared correlation threshold.

W_H multiplies centered edge weights within each edge-set copy. This differs from subtracting the expectation of a raw unsigned subgraph count. The sum uses one copy per subgraph, the outer sum uses one unrooted isomorphism class, and aut(H) supplies an explicit separate weight. Edge-induced subgraphs have no isolated vertices; do not replace them by vertex-induced copies or labeled injections.

q is strictly between0 and1 and the tree size K is an integer with K+1 vertices. Condition(7) requires K→infinity but at most a logarithmic bound with a maximum in its denominator. The sparsity condition is symmetric under q↔1−q. The source states rho²>alpha but does not formulate uniformity for an n-dependent gap shrinking to zero; no boundary-equality claim is inferred.

Definition(1) uses P(f<tau); the two theorem displays use P(f≤tau) while retaining Q(f≥tau). Their bound includes ties on both sides and is sufficient for the strict-event detection definition. Theorem2 inherits tau=C*rho^(2K)*|T| from Theorem1, with fixed0<C<1; it does not use the approximate statistic’s empirical mean or a bootstrap threshold.

P and Q initially name graph-pair laws, but tilde-f also depends on2t independent random colorings. Theorem2 suppresses this extra randomness in its arguments and probability notation. Its natural interpretation extends each data law by the same independent coloring distribution, not a guarantee conditional on every fixed coloring or a data-adaptive coloring scheme.

The approximation uses t=ceil(1/r), two independent arrays of t colorings, and the product of the two sample averages. Arrays are shared across tree classes. Replacing this by the average of t paired products, sharing one coloring array across graphs, omitting a factor r, or resampling edges changes the statistic.

Algorithm1 outputs Y_T, while Theorem2 tests tilde-f_T=beta*Y_T/r². Beta has sign rho^K and the expected exact statistic has rho^(2K); this distinction matters for negative rho. The centered inputs require q, while the normalization/threshold require the stated model parameters; estimating unknown parameters is not covered by these statements.

Theorem2 asserts existence of an n^(2+o(1)) computation with exponential-in-K color coding. Main-text equations(29)–(32) fully define the approximation; the forward reference to appendix equation(54) is not followed. The likelihood-ratio representation, low-degree hardness discussion and Propositions3/4 explain the method or its proof; neither theorem assumes a computational hardness conjecture. The Q transformations in the algebraic conclusions range over O(d), as specified by the preceding setting and G_T definition. They are not arbitrary invertible matrices: diagonal rescalings would otherwise invalidate the conclusion. A maps Y to epsilon, and the surviving ambiguity is left multiplication by signed permutations, changing rows rather than columns.

Equation(10) defines G_T(V) as a subset of O(d), but the following source sentence calls it a subset of Omega, which contains QA. Proposition4.1 gives the actual parameter set Omega_0={QA:Q in G_T(V)}. Preserve the original sentence while keeping transformations Q separate from parameter matrices QA. G_T is not generally a group or the stabilizer of T.

Theorems5.3/5.10 concern arbitrary symmetric tensors, not necessarily realizable as moments/cumulants of a distribution. Theorems5.5/5.14 concern model(1) with centered unit-covariance hidden components and a chosen h_r. No observational-model premise or generating-function existence condition is imported into the algebraic theorems.

h_r denotes either the order-r raw moment tensor or the order-r classical cumulant tensor. Listing both definitions resolves a notation alternative, not a conjunction requiring both tensors to satisfy the restrictions. Their higher-order entries differ; zero mean makes only the third-order tensors coincide. Remark3.1’s extensions are not folded into the default definition.

The source defines moments by expectations and also derivatives of the MGF, and cumulants through log-MGF derivatives. It does not specify a neighborhood where the MGF is finite or analytic. Theorems require the indicated tensors to exist, but finite moments of one order alone do not establish that analytic representation. Preserve this unresolved regularity convention; do not silently assume all moments or replace the original cumulant definition.

For r≥3, Theorem5.3 requires at least d−1 nonzero full diagonal entries, equivalently at most one zero. Its r=2 branch needs pairwise distinct matrix diagonals. For reflectional tensors, condition(14) compares repeated-pair contractions summed over all indices, not just full diagonal entries. These conditions are neither interchangeable nor part of the entrywise zero-pattern definitions.

Definition5.8 permits only the zero tensor at odd order. Theorem5.10 takes even r and l=(r−2)/2, with the standard positive-order context; r=2 yields an empty contraction and distinct diagonal entries. Theorem5.14 does not explicitly exclude r=2, but h_2(epsilon)=I_d under its normalization, so genericity fails for d>1. No new lower bound on r is inserted into the source statement.

Reflectionally invariant means every potentially nonzero entry has even multiplicity of each coordinate label, including off-diagonal pair patterns. It does not mean invariant under every orthogonal transformation. Theorem5.10 describes all transformations into the entire reflectional space, yielding signed permutations; Lemma5.13 describes the smaller exact stabilizer of a fixed generic tensor. The two sets are not merged.

The statistical conclusions determine A from the population distribution up to row sign/permutation, not exact recovery of a unique orientation, a finite-sample estimator or a convergence rate. Neither diagonal constraints at one selected order nor reflectional constraints imply independence. Corollaries for common-variance, elliptical or mean-independent models and later minimum-distance estimation results are not extra Theorems or premises of the general identification statements.

Theorems5.3/5.10 concern arbitrary symmetric tensors, not necessarily realizable as moments/cumulants of a distribution. Theorems5.5/5.14 concern model(1) with centered unit-covariance hidden components and a chosen h_r. No observational-model premise or generating-function existence condition is imported into the algebraic theorems.

h_r denotes either the order-r raw moment tensor or the order-r classical cumulant tensor. Listing both definitions resolves a notation alternative, not a conjunction requiring both tensors to satisfy the restrictions. Their higher-order entries differ; zero mean makes only the third-order tensors coincide. Remark3.1’s extensions are not folded into the default definition.

The source defines moments by expectations and also derivatives of the MGF, and cumulants through log-MGF derivatives. It does not specify a neighborhood where the MGF is finite or analytic. Theorems require the indicated tensors to exist, but finite moments of one order alone do not establish that analytic representation. Preserve this unresolved regularity convention; do not silently assume all moments or replace the original cumulant definition.

For r≥3, Theorem5.3 requires at least d−1 nonzero full diagonal entries, equivalently at most one zero. Its r=2 branch needs pairwise distinct matrix diagonals. For reflectional tensors, condition(14) compares repeated-pair contractions summed over all indices, not just full diagonal entries. These conditions are neither interchangeable nor part of the entrywise zero-pattern definitions.

Definition5.8 permits only the zero tensor at odd order. Reflectionally invariant means every potentially nonzero entry has even multiplicity of each coordinate label, including off-diagonal pair patterns. The statistical conclusions determine A from the population distribution up to row sign/permutation, not exact recovery of a unique orientation, a finite-sample estimator or a convergence rate. The default sphere parameter space contains theta and minus theta. For even f their reward distributions are identical under every adaptive policy, but Definition1 uses expected signed correlation. Thus a uniform signed-correlation guarantee above zero cannot distinguish the two orientations without extra information. No main-text sign-equivalence convention was found. Preserve both the even branch and original loss rather than replacing it with absolute correlation. The source’s appendix-only even-link modifications do not resolve this within the inspected scope.

Definition1 specifies epsilon∈(0,1/2], whereas Definition4 calls Tstar(f,d,1-epsilon) for epsilon∈(0,1/2]. Except at1/2, that argument exceeds the stated Definition1 domain. Preserve this apparent implicit extension. Expected-correlation complexity is distinct from a high-probability path or fixed-prior guarantee.

Theorems1/3 use f-prime although Assumption1 requires only monotonicity. The source explicitly says the general theorem need not assume differentiability and points to finite differences in9. Preserve both forms and flag the derivative interpretation. Flat intervals may make denominators vanish; do not silently assume strict increase or finite complexity.

The introductory model states standard normal noise and history-adapted actions; the sampling algorithms use repeated Gaussian oracle queries, with fresh independent noise understood operationally. Theorem5 instead gives the learner only oracle outputs; online and offline models are alternatives. Theorem10 explicitly removes knowledge of f, overriding the default known-link convention without changing the ridge observation formula.

Theorem4 asserts existence of a bad action tie-breaking rule, not a bound for every tie rule. Theorem5 asserts existence of improper online or proper offline oracle choices that defeat every learner under the corresponding transcript model; it does not quantify over every possible oracle. The main text does not give a complete separate success-probability/minimax definition of Tstar_UCB or Tstar_RO. Improper outputs need not lie on the sphere, leaving f(inner product) outside[-1,1] potentially unresolved.

Assumption2 states differentiability and local derivative bounds near1 but does not explicitly quantify positive c_f,C_f or the range of gamma. Theorems use inverse c_f and positive local intervals, so those conventions are required for nonvacuous rates. Theorem6 adds Assumption1 only for regret; Theorem7 names Assumptions2/3, not1. Do not propagate the scale/even branches into all learning claims.

Algorithm4 lists input correlation≥1-gamma, while Theorem6 supplies the stronger≥1-3gamma/4 used to keep exploration in the local interval. Preserve both. Its budget min(T,d sqrt(T)/c_f) need not be integral and the cyclic design need not complete full coordinate cycles; rounding and small-budget conventions are not specified. The theorem’s ordinary O and proof’s tilde-O notation remain distinct, with no proof-correctness certification.

Theorem9 declares epsilon_i for i≥0 but gives formulas only for1≤i≤m. Algorithm1 runs the firstd0 epochs even ifm<d0; candidate sampling may then have an empty orthogonal sphere in small dimensions. Finite differences may vanish for monotone f. Preserve the original pseudocode, positive-epsilon premise and parameter ranges instead of truncating loops, redefining positivity or inserting unstated large-d conditions.

The function c(.) in Theorem9’s c0 is referenced to Lemma6, which is outside the main text in AppendixA. Its meaning remains unresolved. Algorithm1 uses c0 but its parameter definition can still be archived verbatim. Theorem10’s detailed unknown-link algorithm and the even-link modifications to Algorithm1 are also deferred to excluded appendices. These are recorded limitations, not permission to read appendix bodies.

Theorem8 defines epsilon_t for all t and everydelta∈(0,1), but the default f and g are defined only up to absolute argument1; epsilon1 or later values can exceed1. Theorem11 also maximizes over allK≥1, allowing sqrt(logK/d)>1. No main-text clipping or extension convention was identified. Preserve these formulas and the potentially vacuous1-t delta probability bound without silently extending f.

Theorem8 is a uniform-sphere-prior path bound for any adaptive learner. Theorem11 is a nonadaptive Bayes expected-correlation bound. Theorem12 asserts existence of a hard finite action set at each subexponential K and uses a worst-parameter expectation target≥4/5. Theorem13 instead takes a worst parameter in the unit ball. These scopes and quantifier orders must not be merged into the default Definition1/2 sphere minimax problem.

Theorem13 includes r=0 in a maximum containing f(r)/r^4 or f(r)/r^2 and integrals with zero endpoints. It also uses derivative ratios without stating all positivity/nonzero-domain conventions. Only the monotonicity part of Assumption1 is explicit; the normalized-scale item is not. The displayed bound involving Tf(r) is sensitive to additive shifts of f, unlike regret. Preserve this missing-normalization/endpoint issue rather than adding scale assumptions.

The source defines lesssim/gtrsim/asymp to ignore constant and polylogarithmic factors. Ordinary O is separate. Preserve the source-specific hidden-constant dependencies and distinguish log-squared cost in9 from log-cubed cost in10. Integrals in d(x^2) are not ordinary dx integrals; retain the measure notation.

The general regret display uses max over a-star but evaluates f_theta(a), leaving a free a; Definition2 correctly evaluates the comparator at a-star. Theorem6 describes an achieved algorithm regret using the minimax symbol Rstar. Preserve both original displays and explain the intended comparator/upper-bound roles without rewriting source text.

Enlarged PDF formula crops confirm R0 includes sigma*sqrt(dk)*d_-k, Rcal_k2 begins sqrt(rk)*r_-k and ends sigma*sqrt(dk)*r*T^(-1/2), and Rcal_k1 contains sqrt(dk)*r_-k both in its first and third terms. T3.1/T3.2 print bar-E for the terminal risk but unqualified probability for the joint event, while rate quantities themselves depend on the factor realization. Algorithm1 stops at tolerance or maximum J, but T3.1–T3.3 assert bounds for all m>=0. The source does not explicitly define how iterates are extended after stopping for that universal statement. Keep the recurrence and stopping rule intact; do not manufacture a constant continuation. T3.1/T3.2 use floor, not ceiling, for the displayed terminal J.

T3.3 explicitly names unstarred R0 even though its displayed assumption/conclusion instead use starred R0; retain the named object. It imports rate definitions from T3.1/T3.2, not both full theorem assumption sets. In particular h0<=T/4 is not repeated in T3.3; applicability may rely on surrounding shared conventions, but the missing clause is not inserted into its original statement.

The rates contain inverse lambda or lambda-star and sqrt signal quantities, requiring positive nonzero strengths for finite real evaluation. The displayed general theorems do not add separate rank/ergodicity/mixing assumptions on the factors. Record the formula-domain requirement without importing stronger sufficient hypotheses from subsequent corollaries.

LSVD_m specifies leading singular vectors but no tie-breaking or measurable selection. Algorithm1 prints INIT_k and ITER_k in addition to the operator’s existing k notation. Preserve the formulas and leave selection conventions explicit as ambient requirements for a formal implementation.

iTOPUP uses TOPUP for both steps; iTIPUP uses TIPUP for both; TIPUP-iTOPUP uses TIPUP only for initialization. T3.3 does not supply a theorem for the reverse mixed branch. HOOI appears in comparison and proof motivation, not as the definition of all three procedures.

HypothesisI prints any delta>0 and a limsup of testing risk >1/2; T3.4 invokes it for some delta in(0,1/2). Preserve the wording rather than normalize quantifiers or replace limsup by liminf. Its formal test line says polynomial-time, while preceding prose mentions randomized polynomial time. T3.4 explicitly quantifies randomized estimators.

The lower-bound class has independent factor component series and positive average lag-one moments. It does not say the factor sequence is independent across time; that would conflict with mean zero and positive lag-one moments. Gaussian iid noise entries are explicit in this class, stronger than general Assumption1.

The paper calls a class of tensor data-generating distributions a probability space and writes sample tuples as its members inside the supremum. Preserve the source notation. Sigma_min is globally smallest nontrivial singular value; whether the covariance restriction additionally means full rank is not made explicit by that convention. Estimator orthonormality in the lower-bound quantifiers is inferred from the loading-space estimation task, not restated in the theorem.

Proposition3.1 supplies definitions Rcal_k2/R_TOPUP and a separate guarantee; T3.1 does not import its maxR0=o(1) condition merely by using those definitions. Lemma4.1 is proof-only. Assumption2 and later conditions specialize corollaries; no such assumptions are added to the five Theorems without a statement-level reference.

value.note: Registered source is arXiv2410.04384v1 marked6Oct2024,25pages. Main text ends after acknowledgements on24, before the supplementary-material notice at y395.594; evidence clipped390. The notice points to a separate supplement, whose bodies are excluded. Exactly seven actual Theorems are retained.

T6.1 requires Assumption1 and supplementary S2–S4, described only as adaptations of Assumptions3–4. T6.2 inherits those assumptions. The supplement remains out of scope, so their precise content and dependency closure are unresolved. Neither theorem is dropped or treated as assumption-free; the original references and limits are explicit.

Assumption1 writes rho(t) with an outer supremum over s,t>=1, reusing the lag variable, and writes f andg as members of sigma-fields rather than specifying measurable finite-variance random variables. It calls F_(t-1) the filtration generated by data through index t including current covariates. Preserve these source conventions without rewriting the definition. Theorems3.1/3.2 retain the printed geometric assumption despite prose suggesting a polynomial relaxation.

Boundary first coordinates are fixed to1, so their estimation differences have zero first coordinates. D(v) is nevertheless declared on R^(d1+d2) and uses only v_-1,i. The source does not restrict the two redundant coordinates or specify intrinsic measure for centroid integration. Taking the written full-space domain literally leaves free directions and prevents the stated ordinary full-volume centroid construction.

The paper asserts strict convexity in beta, a unique beta minimizer, identical optimal partitions and a convex boundary-minimizer set. These assertions are not assured for arbitrary finite samples with empty/rank-deficient cells or tied partitions, and compact Gamma/B need not be convex. Preserve them as source assertions, not certified general properties. Compactness with discontinuous indicators also does not alone guarantee an attained minimum.

Region definitions assign equality to nonpositive sides. The later expression product 1(s_j*z_j^T gamma_j>0) omits equality even when s_j=-1, whereas its claimed binary expression uses g_j=0 for nonpositive values. The mismatch occurs exactly on candidate boundaries. The source MIQP constraints themselves retain their original strict and non-strict sides.

Gamma_i andB are only specified as compact, while the source calls the constraints linear/polyhedral and M_jt computable by linear programming. Additional polyhedral assumptions are not printed. Strict inequalities are not standard closed MIQP constraints; solver epsilon/tolerance substitutions are not part of Theorem4.1. Epsilon in(4.3)/(4.7) expands a negative bound and does not impose a positive margin on g=1.

Retain the boundary-coefficient set’s i/j mismatch, missing comma between(2,1) and(3,4) inS(1), extra commas in Assumption3 andT3.1, missing indicator parentheses in covariance definitions and(6.2), and brace notation R2{gamma0}. Formula delimiters remain as printed where they can be represented directly in LaTeX; no change in mathematical meaning is asserted.

Assumptions4/5 condition on hyperplanes or q_i=0, typically probability-zero events. The source asks continuity and bounds for some conditional densities but does not fully specify common versions for every conditional moment or support point. Preserve the original conditional clauses and their almost-sure/pointwise qualifiers.

Assumption5(i) quantifies one fixed positive delta3 and a constant bound on paired-neighborhood probabilities. The surrounding prose describes a smaller-order rare-event effect, but the printed condition has no delta→0 uniformity. Do not replace it by a stronger shrinking-threshold condition.

In(3.4), the indicator requires0<J while J=s^(k)_i times a positive exponential sum divided by a positive density. Negative-sign families therefore have no contribution in the printed expression. The paper describes a multivariate compound Poisson process covering boundary directions; a missing complementary orientation may be intended, but no term is invented or read from a supplementary proof.

The centroid integral needs positive finite volume in a specified dimension. Normalized parameter spaces can have zero ambient volume, and the limiting process domain has unremoved free directions. Averaging N arbitrary minimizers or solver outputs is not automatically an unbiased/consistent centroid approximation. The source acknowledges the solver sampling mechanism is unknown and does not state an N→infinity rate alongside B,T→infinity inT5.1.

Equation5.1 prints beta_0 rather than beta_k0 inside the regime sum, even though beta_0 earlier denotes the stacked coefficients. The fitted-residual line similarly omits the t index onX and the k index on fitted beta. Preserve these expressions and their apparent dimension/index gaps; the actual resampling Step1 separately prints beta-hat_k correctly.

G_i is defined by integrating a density from minus infinity up to u, but F0-tilde uses(X_t-x)/h1 and(Z_t-z)/h2. For positive bandwidths this is decreasing in evaluation coordinates, unlike a usual CDF. Preserve the source expression and record that resampling from it as an ordinary distribution needs clarification; do not reverse the arguments silently.

The model allows shared covariates and definesZ as the union of variables inZ1/Z2. Later kernels treatZ as dimensiond1+d2 and demand an absolutely continuous joint law of(X,Z), which fails in redundant ambient coordinates when variables coincide. Assumption6 also combines compact support with a positive infimum over unqualified all(x,z); the intended support-relative domain is not explicitly supplied.

Assumption6 bounds the true variance above and away from0 but does not print continuity/smoothness assumptions for that function, despite claiming uniform consistency of its local-linear estimate. Local-linear fitted variances can be nonpositive; no truncation or denominator convention is stated before standardized residuals are formed. These are source limitations, not extra hypotheses imposed by the census.

Step1 calls the covariate law F-tilde while the preceding definition isF0-tilde. The standardized empirical residual law G-hat is different from calligraphicG-hat for boundary minimizers. Resampling is independent even though original data are dependent; this is the stated model-based construction, not a block bootstrap. LT,B uses finite-N boundary averages while LT is written using the original centroid.

In family(a.2), the source uses z_i^T gamma_j,0, which may have incompatible dimensions when di!=dj, and its printed R2 is a subset ofR3 rather than a disjoint region. Figure1(C) labels R2 as(-,+), while the printed inequalities differ. Preserve both source representations and leave the intended correction unresolved.

Earlier G-hat is the set of all stacked boundary minimizers; Section6 reuses it for the finite set of two fitted boundary vectors. Point-to-set distance is Euclidean and unsquared. If d1!=d2, the finite set contains differently sized vectors, and the source does not state how invalid comparisons are omitted. The original L0=1/L0=2 cases are retained separately.

The recursive algorithm defines an initial ST(4) with a free K in the inner sum, later lists ST(K) only forK=2,3,4 though the final minimum includes1, and freely relabels merged regions. The recurrence does reachK=1, but no matching permutation with true region labels is specified forT6.2’s per-k conclusion. The theorem inheritsK0<4 fromT6.1, even though surrounding text discusses selecting up to four regimes.

Regime error bounds use ordinaryO(1/T) although estimated regions are random; the source does not explicitly specify conditional versus integrated probability over a newZ and fitted data. T6.2 writes P{estimated-region triangle true-region} without Z membership. Preserve this implicit set-probability notation and the original O versusOp distinction.

n equals the number of grid points inOmega; delta is small enough for16 and n>=2. C_(k,h) partitions grid intersections, not necessarily every point ofOmega. F^frakturL bounds the unsquared empirical distance to all affine functions. It is design-dependent and allows unbounded affine trends. Do not substitute a Lipschitz bound, uniform bound, or a squared-distance threshold. The supremum class and the unrestricted estimator class are different.

N1 is conditional mean zero andN2 is a conditional second-moment upper bound in every fixed direction, not covariance equality or merely a marginal bound. Functional5 usesSigma_w inverse, so its ordinary formula requires positive definiteness or a separately supplied extension. ForSigma_w=0 admissible noiseless observations exist but that formula is undefined; no pseudoinverse convention is stated. The open feasible set need not attain its supremum; Section2.1 explicitly discusses approximating sequences.

Error is measured withK_e, parameter norm withK_c inverse, and trace budget withK_c inverse square roots. The matrix products cannot be reordered by assuming commutativity. The estimator output need not lie inTheta. Theorem2 halves the radius, notK_c, the noise variance, or the constant alone.

Omega is deterministic and selected before averaging overxi. T_xi has no moment/rank assumption in the general setup, so17 may require extended-value/integrability interpretation. For the well-defined positive-definite noise case, the inverse in5 is bounded in PSD order byOmega, keepingPhi finite under its trace budget.

Only four actual Theorem environments, numbered 4–7, occur in the main text; Propositions 1–3 and 8 are not Theorems. All supplementary bodies are excluded.

Conditional mean independence is the null of Theorems 4 and 6. Full conditional independence is stronger and is required only by alternative (ii) of Theorem 4. No parametric linear-model equivalence from the earlier proposition discussion is imported into this model-free null.

The page 16 introductory prose lists mhat and mhatf then D3 and D4 without an explicit respectively. The operative Algorithm 2 assigns step 3(i), the projection regression, to D3 and step 3(ii), the response regression, to D4. D1 evaluates the statistic; D2 trains the projection. Theorem 7 excludes the D3=D4 relaxation. n is per split, not the total sample size.

Conditioning on hatf includes the training sample and any algorithmic randomness. epsilon_P is Y-m_P(Z), even under alternatives; xi_P is hatf minus its population regression on Z, not the fitted regression. sigma_P² is the conditional variance of xi_P. Assumption 4(a) uses this response residual, not Y-g_P(X,Z).

The source explicitly sets 0/0=0 and sgn(0)=0. Theorem 4(a) asymptotically excludes exact sigma_P²=0 but does not impose a fixed positive variance lower bound. Algorithm 1 can permit fitted variance zero. The source does not fully specify all nonzero-over-zero, infinite-product, or degenerate conditional correlation conventions; retain the formulas and do not silently supply a totalization beyond its stated zero rule.

Part (b) is printed as sup_P h_P(X,Z)<=C, without absolute values and without an explicit new quantifier for C. Preserve that one-sided condition rather than replacing it by a uniform absolute bound or claiming the proof has been checked. The conditional correlation lower bound in (d) is positive and need not tend to one.

The spline results use vhat identically one, OLS on phi for ghat, phi^Z for mtilde and the higher-order psi for the two final regressions. The sign correction is omitted because rhohat is nonnegative. Algorithm 1 remains the base procedure; its general variance-estimation step is overridden, not a separate requirement of Theorems 6/7.

The source defines u tensor v as vec(uv transpose); preserve its block indexing and Pi subtraction. Pi removes within-X means separately for each Z-basis block. Theorem 6 restricts the covariance Rayleigh quotient to Pi x=x. Precise endpoint and repeated-knot conventions are in excluded Section S4; no arbitrary implementation is supplied.

Assumption 4(a) says for each P, the conditional second moment lower bound holds and there exists delta in (0,2] giving the higher moment bound. Theorem 6 then uses delta from Assumption 4 in a single growth condition. Whether a common delta is intended is not explicitly resolved by this wording; retain the printed order and flag the uniformity issue. Conditional density smoothness is in z for each fixed x; g is smooth in all d coordinates.

Sufficient stability is defined by Proposition S15(ii),(iii), and precise Holder spaces/norms by Definition S24; detailed spline construction is in S4. These are definition references, not merely proof citations. Their main-text pointers are saved but the excluded bodies are not read or reconstructed.

Theorem 6 has two additional rate requirements and a nondegeneracy condition; Theorem 7 has different tuning/separation and needs separate auxiliary training. Do not propagate the generic Assumption 3 or sufficient-stability condition as added hypotheses of these spline theorems. Theorem 7 knows s; it does not prove adaptation, and its alpha range comes from Algorithm 2.

value.note: Registered arXiv2210.08571v3 is stamped19June2025, title date23June2025,86pages. It is a revision of the2024 article. Six Theorems occur in main text, including6 in the proof section. Main text ends beforeReferences on34; all appendices beginning38 are excluded.

Ridge inverse formulas are for lambda>0; ridgeless is a positive limit. In the underparameterized case the effective root tends to zero and Theorem4 conditions zero bias on rank(X)=d. Do not assume all random designs are full rank or use a singular ordinary inverse atzero. Assumption1 permits covariance zeros; d>n and sigma_n>0 do not alone force covariance rank>n, so the asserted positive lambda_star(0) and positive C_Sigma may need additional support-rank conditions.

The inverse-covariance norm and theta=Sigma^-1/2 beta require a domain/nullspace convention when covariance has zero eigenvalues or an unbounded inverse. The source does not fully specify that convention. The directional ratio normalizes by||theta||², undefined atzero signal absent a separate convention; preserve the limitation rather than deleting a stated signal condition.

Trace-class covariance permits H-valued features in infinite dimensions, but their isotropic whitened coordinate sequence need not be square summable. The main text gives a finite-projection extension for concentration; do not reinterpret z as an H-valued isotropic vector with finite trace covariance.

Assumption1II(a) allows independent non-identically distributed standardized coordinates; II(b) allows dependence with convex concentration. These are alternatives, not joint Gaussianity or concentration for every Lipschitz function. Whitening/support isotropy conventions under a singular covariance remain implicit.

d_Sigma(n) is an admissible envelope>=n, with tails including k, not an exact minimized quantity. Theorem2 uses sigma_2n and sigma_floor(eta*n); Theorem3 uses sigma_(C5*n) and sigma_d even for potentially infinite d. Finite-rank zero extensions, noninteger rounding and sigma_infinity conventions are not explicitly given in those statements; retain these source limitations.

Theorem3 uses P(A^c intersect E)<=Delta, not a conditional probability given E. Its final spectral lower bound has a separate probability statement. The bias error includes a minimum of two additive bounds, in addition to a relative B_n term; it is not wholly multiplicative.

Positive-ridge kappa is the interior ratio in25; ridgeless kappa is a free positive parameter constrained inTheorem3. Theorem2 nu is lambda/lambda_star while Theorem4 nu is min(d/n,1-d/n). Do not merge these merely because symbols recur. Zero-limit trace equations require a limiting interpretation.

Theorem2 states suppression of C,Cprime,epsilon while the optional signal bound uses Cdoubleprime; its precise dependence is not fully restated. Theorem4 uses k,D without newly quantifying them, and epsilon is only stated positive although useful rates require its exponent regime. Preserve original wording and inherited context rather than silently rewriting quantifiers.

Theorem5 permits an arbitrary slowly varying factor in sigma_i but evaluates lambda_star and actual risk at nu*n^(-alpha), while its proposed limit constants depend on nu as though the regularization were scaled by sigma_n. A varying slow factor changes that effective ratio. In branch2 a_i can converge to a positive constant different from1, creating a related scale issue. Preserve the printed formulas; do not silently replace their arguments by nu*sigma_n or assert the formulas are proved correct.

The two F_beta measures use floor(n*x) and floor((n/log n)*x), respectively; both depend onn. The scalar decay exponent theta is distinct from the bold inverse-covariance signal theta. c_star is defined separately in each spectral branch. The optional bias predicates remain tied to their own branches.

Script R_n is a covariance-resolvent trace, plain R_n is total effective prediction risk, and sans-serif R0 is a local shorthand inTheorem6. Its general mu_star parameter need not obey the positive-ridge kappa/rho conditions. Keep1+R0(I)^2 distinct from(1+R0(I))² in the error parameters. No proof-only theta normalization or ridge learner/noise requirement is added to the design-only resolvent conclusion.

Hanson–Wright lemmas, equivalent Gaussian sequence model, application Proposition hypotheses, finite-difference lemmas, filtrations and proof normalization are not extra requirements of every theorem. Theorem6 itself is retained because it is a labeled main-text Theorem. Source review certifies extraction fidelity and dependency scope, not proof validity.

items.value: Ten notes preserve the registered manuscript version, first-change indexing, the contradictory exact-block-boundary convention, arbitrary versus specific variance estimation, overlapping-window normalization, ties and empty minima, finite-sample division problems, distinct dependence parameters and rates, optional defaults and proof/application scope.

value.note: Registered arXiv2409.08863v1, stamped13September2024,39pages. Main text ends after acknowledgments/funding on16. Supplementary availability listings and references occupy17–18; appendix bodies start19 and are excluded. Exactly three main-text Theorems3.1–3.3; Corollary3.1 is not inventoried.

Tau denotes the first changed observation, so pre-change means stop at tau-1 and the final argmin sums through j-1. d is a positive lower bound for all post-change gaps, not necessarily the attained minimum. d_star averages the signal over sliding blocks; d_hat estimates that averaged quantity. Preserve the strict d>K*d_star inequality with K>rho; feasibility with d_star>=d implies K<1 rather than an arbitrary large constant.

The source defines eta=floor(tau/k) and also calls it the last fully pre-change block, writing eta*k+1<=tau<=(eta+1)*k. At tau exactly divisible byk, that interval is inconsistent and the eta-th block includes the first changed observation. Retain the literal floor definition and the contradictory prose; do not silently substitute floor((tau-1)/k).

Definitions(5) and(9) permit any consistent long-run-variance estimator; estimator(8) is a suggested canonical choice. Theorem3.2 supplies a rate for(8) under its own stronger moment/block/gap conditions. These do not become mandatory premises ofTheorem3.1, and Theorem3.3 does not require that its user-chosen variance estimate be(8). The mean muhat0 from(8) is still a required preliminary mean for(9).

R_(s/k) extends nonoverlapping R_j to sliding windows even for noninteger s/k. The variance estimate uses k/(ellhat-k+1), all endpoints s=k..ellhat and centering by the entire selected-prefix mean. It is not an average over only the original disjoint block means.

Argmin tie-breaking for L_hat, eta_hat and tau_hat is not stated. The optional fixed-J max-index selection is not a general tie convention. For finite data, eta_hat=m-1 is allowed by(10) but makes the sliding-window range in d_hat empty; no fallback is supplied. High-probability asymptotics do not by themselves define these bad finite-sample outputs.

Population long-run variance is explicitly positive and finite. Generic consistent estimates can still be zero or negative on finite-sample events; estimator(8) is nonnegative but can be zero. The source does not fully specify square-root/sign/zero-division conventions. m>=2 is needed for the interior normal quantile and step-fit range, and follows eventually from the stated growth regime.

Functional dependence replaces only innovation0 by an independent copy. Cumulative dependence sums over future indices, while long-run covariance sums over all integer lags. Condition3.1 retains both theta regimes and the exact gamma_theta radical/log threshold; gamma_theta is not the autocovariance gamma(k). The same theta must satisfy all moment, signal and block-rate conditions.

Theorem3.2 has separate deterministic and probabilistic error terms. Theorem3.3 uses d_star with negative exponent theta/(theta-1). Rho=1/2, block length ceil(n^(1/3)) and geometric moment contraction are optional examples, not universal hypotheses. Early and late changes are allowed; tau need not be proportional ton.

Brownian-bridge limits and KMT coupling interpret or prove the statistical results, not extra assumptions on observed noise. Oracle true-gap estimator(21) is not the actual estimator(12). Appendix proofs are excluded. The empirical interpretation of a search-index change as an epidemic starting date is application context and is not certified by this theorem census.

items.value: Nineteen source notes retain matrix-dimension conventions, endpoint and time-zero ambiguities, referenced conditional assumptions, derivative-variable and aggregate-noise bindings, cross-client sampling, window/segment and clipping conditions, scalar/matrix Hessian distinctions and the uppercase F_k notation in Theorem 6. Three unresolved source-ambiguity records remain explicit; none is represented as corrected or proven.

value.note: Page 4 defines J=d^{-1}*1_d*1_d^T, but the right-centering matrix in Theta_hat_t*(I-J) must act on K client columns. Page 6 explicitly uses K^{-1}*1_K*1_K^T. Preserve both source passages and record the dimension mismatch; do not silently replace d by K inside the quoted definition.

Assumption 2.1 permits rho=0, and Theorem 1 evaluates delta at rho^(1/tau) and its square, while its printed delta definition says a in (0,1). The following remark uses the natural a=0 interpretation. Preserve the open domain and document that extension separately.

Theorem 1 at t=tau invokes eta_floor((t-tau+1)/2)=eta_0 although Assumption 2.2 introduces the sequence for t>=1. An empty sum occurs for tau=1. Record these finite-index conventions rather than silently adding values.

The remark after Theorem 1 changes the order of delta arguments and calls it (14), although equation (14) is the curvature condition. Keep the theorem formula delta(t,a,tau) and distinguish the remark typo.

Assumption 3.4(ii) prints phi triple-prime at t and phi double-prime at u without a full relation or quantifier for t; it also omits an absolute value on the third derivative. Preserve the original condition and record its ambiguity rather than substituting a standard self-concordance definition.

Assumption 3.4 has alternative strong-convexity and bounded-domain generalized self-concordance cases. Do not require the bounded-domain assumptions jointly with the positive-mu case. Theorem 5 separately requires a bounded domain in all cases.

Theorems 3, 4 and 6 refer to assumptions of Theorem 2. Resolve the common assumptions and retain its part-(ii) conditional step-size restrictions as referenced context; inspect the source carefully before deciding their scope. Do not import its fixed-K almost-sure conclusion as a premise.

Theorem 5 explicitly uses v=2 and lists 3.3–3.4 without 3.2. It nevertheless assumes 4.1, described by the author as stronger smoothness. Preserve the printed list; do not insert an unstated numbered assumption merely to match the other theorems.

Page 3 specifies IID observations within each client, while the covariance aggregation on page 12 uses the no-cross-client-covariance formula. Check whether cross-client independence is explicitly stated elsewhere in the main text; record any missing joint-sampling premise rather than inventing it.

Assumption 4.2 mixes notation for aggregated noise epsilon(theta) and epsilon(theta;xi^k), though epsilon(theta) itself sums noises from all clients. Retain its original variables and record the binding issue.

Equation (22) uses gradients at local estimate theta_hat_t^k and data xi_t^k with t=0..T-1; the update (6) uses theta_hat_(t-1)^k and xi_t^k with t>=1. Retain the original covariance-estimator indexing and inspect the time-zero/data-reuse issue.

The trailing-window Hessian estimator (24) uses a(T) observations but only states that a is positive integer-valued and nondecreasing; a(T)<=T is not explicit. Its local temporal mean also reaches index zero when the window spans all observations. Preserve the formula and note any undefined early indices.

In (31), r1+r2+r3=T is imposed, but for alpha=1 the printed r1=T^(1-zeta)/C2 and r2=T/C3, r3=T/C4 with fixed constants cannot sum to T for all T. Integer rounding is also unspecified. Preserve the original formulas without silently changing constants or a segment.

Thresholded V clips eigenvalues to [delta,1/delta] for a small fixed delta>0. The source does not explicitly state a relation between that interval and the limiting spectrum in the theorem. Record that limitation rather than assuming clipping becomes asymptotically inactive.

The regression Hessian estimator Z*V^{-1} need not be symmetric at finite T. The later sandwich formula repeats its inverse without a transpose, as printed. Keep original formulas and distinguish an estimator definition from a claim of finite-sample symmetry.

Equation (33) uses lowercase f_k with a data argument, but Theorem 6 prints uppercase F_k(theta_K*;xi_t^k), although F_k was defined as a population risk with only a parameter argument. Preserve the printed theorem and record the apparent notation error separately.

Theorem 6 expansion has remainder O_p(sqrt(K/T)+1/sqrt(K)); its CLT consequence requires both K and T to diverge. Do not extend it to fixed K based on the PR theorem, which permits fixed K under a different step-size regime.

The external supplement contains algorithm summaries, proofs and sparse-network variants. Main-text algorithm definitions are available and should be used directly. Do not read supplement bodies or add their results to the main-text theorem inventory.

The target is defined by constrained minimization over closed convex Phi. The main-text definition does not separately state an interior-target or unconstrained-stationarity condition. Preserve the stated asymptotic normality and record this domain issue rather than silently assuming a zero gradient at every constrained minimizer.

Theorem 1 prints a zero block of dimension [p_b:1] in the second row of F_{1(a),(b)}, alongside a [p_a:p_b] block. The row dimensions appear inconsistent when p_a differs from p_b. The quoted theorem retains this dimension.
The eta=infinity reordering prints sigma_a^2 with a Latin a and calls the covariance an asymptotic coavriate matrix. These original tokens are retained without correcting the source statement.

All four printed variance derivatives of the adjusted likelihood have minus one-half trace corrections. Differentiating the preceding minus log-determinant expression instead yields plus corrections. The objective and printed score are both preserved; which formulation was intended requires clarification.

Do not replace the abbreviated source convention with an uninspected appendix formula.

Condition A4 uses enlarged capital-X Gram matrices for the row, column and interaction limits, whereas D1-D4 are the indicated diagonal blocks. Preserve this distinction and the separate lowercase-x moment conditions.

The model does not assume Gaussian truth: Condition A3 supplies independent families with finite 4+delta moments. The covariance includes third moments and excess fourth moments; an information-equality Gaussian covariance is not an equivalent replacement.
